result.topic_en: Riemann's draft notes on the conditions for the convergence of a trigonometric series at a point x=a, using the second-difference quotient F(x+α)-2F(x)+F(x-α), the integrability of f(a+t)+f(a-t) near t=0, and Dirichlet's integral \int f(x)\sin n(x-a)dx/(x-a).

items.english: This condition suffices for \int_{a+ε}^c f(x) sin n(x-a) dx to become infinitely small as ε decreases and n eventually increases.

For functions without infinitely many maxima and minima, it is necessary and sufficient for representability by a trigonometric series with coefficients decreasing to zero as n→∞ that, if the function becomes infinite at x=a, f(a+t)t and f(a-t)t become infinitely small with t and f(a+t)+f(a-t) can be integrated up to t=0.

items.english: If a function f(x) without infinitely many maxima and minima does not satisfy these conditions, then in a trigonometric series which represents the function where it converges, the terms would not [eventually become infinitely small]...
